vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: topclawhubskills
Version: 1.0.0

The skill is designed to interact with an external API at `https://topclawhubskills.com/api` to retrieve information about ClawHub skills. All described API interactions are read-only GET requests, and the instructions in `SKILL.md` guide the agent on how to query this API and format the results. There is no evidence of prompt injection attempts, data exfiltration, malicious execution, persistence mechanisms, or other harmful behaviors. The external network calls are central to the skill's stated purpose and do not appear to be used for unauthorized activities.

llm.summary: The skill's instructions and required capabilities largely match its stated purpose (query a public API and format results), but the publisher/source is unknown, there is no homepage or repo, and the SKILL.md relies on an external domain (https://topclawhubskills.com) with a small endpoint inconsistency — these provenance gaps and external-network behavior merit caution before installing.

dimensions.detail: Name and description match the instructions: the skill only documents how to call a public API to list/popularize ClawHub skills and how to format results. However, the SKILL.md declares an external domain (topclawhubskills.com) with no homepage or source repository provided, which reduces provenance and trust. Also the declared API base URL includes '/api' and each endpoint path also starts with '/api', creating an inconsistent/duplicated path (likely a small bug but worth noting).
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Instructions are narrow and limited to making HTTP GET requests to the documented endpoints and formatting the returned JSON into Markdown. The instructions do not ask the agent to read local files, environment variables, or other system state. They do require contacting an external third-party API, which will reveal request metadata (IP, query terms) to that domain. The duplicated '/api' in base URL vs endpoints is an inconsistency that could cause incorrect requests.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec and no code files — instruction-only skill. This minimizes disk write/execution risk because nothing is installed by the skill itself.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill requests no environment variables, no credentials, and no config paths. The lack of requested secrets is proportionate to its stated purpose of fetching public listing data.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false and default agent invocation settings. The skill does not request permanent presence or elevated privileges. Autonomous invocation is allowed (platform default) but not combined with other concerning flags.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to simply read public listing data from an external API and format it, which is coherent with its name — but there are two reasons to be cautious before enabling it: 1) provenance: there is no homepage, source repository, or publisher information beyond an owner ID, so you can't verify who runs the API or their trustworthiness; 2) privacy/networking: using the skill causes your agent to make outbound HTTPS requests to topclawhubskills.com, which reveals that you queried these endpoints (your IP, request timing, and query terms). Recommendations: - Ask the publisher for a homepage or source repo (GitHub) and confirm the API operator before installing. - Manually test the API (e.g., curl https://topclawhubskills.com/api/health) in a sandbox to inspect responses and TLS certificate. - Verify the endpoint path (the SKILL.md base URL includes '/api' and endpoints also include '/api'; confirm correct URL). - If you are privacy-sensitive, run the skill behind a proxy or in an environment that hides your agent's network identity, or avoid installing until provenance is established. - Treat the security certification claim in the doc as a marketing statement until you can validate the cert process or evidence.
